title: Construction of a Near-IR-Luminescent Rectangular Yb(III) Complex from a Dodecadentate Schiff Base Ligand for the Excitation-Wavelength-Dependent Detection of Aloe Emodin (a Natural Medicinal Ingredient)

synthesis.procedure: Yb(NO3)3·5H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.0898 g) and H6L (0.10 mmol, 0.0883 g) were dissolved in EtOH (4 mL), MeOH (6 mL), and DMF (2 mL) at room temperature, then a solution of triethylamine in EtOH (1.0 mol/L, 2 mL) was added. The mixture was stirred and heated under reflux for 30 min, cooled, and filtered. Diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature, giving red crystals after three weeks. The crystals were filtered, washed with EtOH (3 × 5 mL), and dried in air for one day.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature, then reflux, then room-temperature vapor diffusion
synthesis.time: reflux 30 min; crystallization 3 weeks; air drying 1 day
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reflux followed by diethyl ether vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled and filtered; slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate at room temperature afforded red crystals after three weeks; crystals washed with EtOH (3 × 5 mL) and dried in air for one day

properties.summary: Octanuclear complex 1 shows ligand-sensitized NIR Yb(III) emission at 980 nm. Aloe emodin quenches this emission under 395 nm excitation (LOD 1.19 μM) and enhances it under 500 nm excitation (LOD 0.048 nM); the dual-wavelength intensity ratio was used to quantify aloe emodin, including in fetal calf serum and commercial aloe soft capsules.
